title: Niche Burn Buffer & Headcount Pricing Sensitivity Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working playbook combining a small, targeted burn buffer (narrowband reserve) with headcount phasing and per-feature pricing sensitivity. Goal: produce pragmatic trigger rules and a lightweight proforma we can run during a mid-cycle price shock or product-led usage spike.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Build a 12-week narrowband burn buffer equal to 14% of current committed spend to cover 2x usage volatility for priority features (chat, embeddings).
- Prioritize hiring freezes for non-critical roles and accelerate two SRE contractors for burst capacity instead of permanent hires in Q3.
- Implement a three-tier price sensitivity test (0%, +10%, +25%) on the Starter slab / burst pricing for on-demand customers and simulate headcount and revenue feedback loops.
- Trigger points: if 7-day token growth >+23% week-over-week and gross margin compression >3pp vs plan, enact Tier B actions within 5 business days.

Context and motivation:
- We have observed short-duration spikes in tokens from a handful of accounts (embed-heavy) that blow past our slab assumptions and force spot-burst GPU use. Historically this drives both cost and SRE load.
- Senior leadership wants a minimally invasive buffer that avoids knee-jerk pricing moves for customers while protecting runway.
- This doc sits between the high-level scenario planning (see CONFLUENCE-6178) and the execution runbooks (JIRA-FIN-892).

Key assumptions (base case):
- Baseline committed monthly spend (hosted API revenue) = $8.2M ARR (approx $683k MRR baseline).
- Typical token mix: 62% generation/chat, 28% embeddings, 10% other (reranking, evals).
- Unit cost profile (tokens): gen 0.0009 USD/token, embed 0.00015 USD/unit (simplified).
- Hiring/triage lag: 8–12 weeks from req to fully productive IC. Contractors: 2–4 weeks.

Scenarios and quick proforma (text table):
- Scenario A (mild): +15% 90-day token growth concentrated in embeddings. Impact: +6% gross cost, translate to -1.2pp GM.
- Scenario B (medium): +40% 90-day token growth cross-product. Impact: +18% gross cost, -3.8pp GM.
- Scenario C (severe): +85% 90-day token growth with >60% from top 5 customers. Impact: +36% gross cost, -7.2pp GM.

Planned buffer sizing rationale:
- Narrowband buffer = 14% of committed spend = roughly $96k/month equivalent (14% * $683k). Reasoning: covers ~2x volatility on high-cost gen tokens for 6–8 weeks without permanent capacity changes.
- Maintain buffer as a combination: 60% cash reserve, 40% contractor/pre-negotiated spot credit (vendor).

Headcount phasing (text-based table):
- Q2 (now -> end Q2): pause 2 open PM roles; move $60k/month hiring allocation into buffer. Fill 1 SRE contractor (4-week ramp).
- Q3 (start): convert 50% of contractor time to permanent only if rolling 8-week burn < buffer and GM delta < 1pp.
- Q4 contingency: if Scenario C persists >12 weeks, initiate 1.5% company-wide salary deferral (discuss with People Ops).

Pricing sensitivity test (framework):
- Test axes: Starter slab price bump (+10% tokens price), Burst surcharge (new temporary 20% uplift for on-demand sessions >X tokens), and Volume rebate cap changes.
- Experiment cohorts: 20% of Starter customers (randomized) for +10% price A/B for 6 weeks; 10% cohort for +25% (higher-risk cohort, opt-in for pilots).
- Metrics to track: take-rate movement, churn in cohort, net revenue retention (NRR) change, token displacement to other providers (qualitative via CS).

Pricing sensitivity model outputs (notes from quick sims):
- +10% price on Starter: projected immediate revenue +6% but cancels out ~1.8% of demand in 90 days; net revenue +3.9% (base case elasticities).
- +25% price: immediate revenue +18% but demand drop of ~7% -> net +9% but increased churn risk among price-sensitive SMBs.
- Burst surcharge: modest revenue uplift (projected +2% total) and strong cost signal reducing abuse. Operational complexity: billing changes and docs update needed, 3-week engineering lift.

Trigger rules and playbook (actionable):
- Monitoring inputs (owners): 7d token growth (Analytics), 14d gross margin delta (Finance), top-10 customer token concentration (Customer Success).
- Thresholds:
  * Green: 7d growth < +10% and GM delta < 1pp -> no action.
  * Amber: 7d growth between +10% and +23% or GM delta between 1–3pp -> pre-authorize contractor burn (Finance ok), freeze non-essential hiring, notify GTM.
  * Red: 7d growth > +23% or GM delta > 3pp OR top-5 customer concentration > 50% -> implement pricing Tier B (temporary +10% Starter uplift for new signups + activate burst surcharge), schedule emergency exec review within 48 hours.
- Communication plan: Finance drafts customer-facing short note (CS) + internal FAQ. Legal loop: 24-hour turnaround for contract impact check.

Operational notes / engineering impact:
- Burst surcharge requires: billing change, telemetry flag, docs update, SDK notes. Estimate 1.8 FTE-weeks cross-team.
- Quick win: ramp prefix/KV cache tweaks for top embed-heavy customers — SRE to pilot for top 3 accounts (low-effort, high-impact).

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Need per-region cost multiplier for EU vs US GPUs (ask Infra for updated spot premiums).
- Confirm whether existing Dedicated reserved pools can be temporarily reallocated for hosted customers without SLA break — ping product/infra.
- Get more granular elasticity by customer cohort (SMB vs enterprise) — request data from Analytics (CONFLUENCE-6178: dataset export).

Appendix: quick calcs (rough):
- Monthly buffer estimate = 0.14 * 683,000 = $95,620
- If Scenario B: incremental monthly cost = 0.18 * base_cost; base_cost approximated at 28% of revenue = 0.28 * 683,000 = $191,240 -> incremental = $34,423/month -> buffer covers ~2.8 months of incremental cost at buffer size.

References and artifacts:
- CONFLUENCE-6178: mid-cycle pricing playbook (link above)
- JIRA-FIN-892: buffer funding approval ticket
- PR: prod-costing/pull/42 for initial billing prototype
- Slack thread: #finance-weekly-thread May 13 conversation with Product on burst surcharge

Version notes: draft v0.2 — working numbers, leaning conservative on buffer. Next steps: finalize sensitivity sim with Analytics (due 2026-06-09), align with Product on billing feasibility (EOW 2026-06-04), and assemble exec one-pager for review (target 2026-06-11).

Quick sign-off checklist (owner: Aisha):
- [ ] Analytics runs cohort elasticity by 6/9
- [ ] Infra confirms region multipliers by 6/5
- [ ] Legal pre-checks contract impacts by 6/7
- [ ] Draft customer comms w/CS by 6/8
